headline: Tessera CFO Found Dead; Red Ledger Claims Responsibility
body:
Tessera Corporation's Chief Financial Officer Ingrid Solberg-Faye, 54, was found dead in her secured residence on the 91st floor of the Tessera Spire at approximately 0340 this morning. Municipal Enforcement confirmed the death and described evidence of a 'targeted professional action,' declining to elaborate. A message bearing the Red Ledger cipher signature — a mark attributed to a contract assassination network active in Meridian 88 since at least 2119 — was transmitted to three press outlets simultaneously at 0600, stating that Solberg-Faye had been 'debited for debts accrued.' No further explanation was given.

Solberg-Faye oversaw Tessera's financial architecture during the corponation's contentious 2134-2136 restructuring, which saw over 12,000 workers involuntarily delisted from Tessera's internal citizen registry — stripping them of housing credits, medical access, and pension rights in a single administrative action. The Collective filed forty-seven grievances over the delistings; all were dismissed under Tessera's internal sovereignty protocols. 'Nobody at Tessera is surprised,' said one Tessera mid-tier employee, speaking anonymously. 'Surprised it took this long, maybe.'

Solberg-Faye had been under the protection of an Arcturus Defense private security detail rated for corporate-tier threats. MME sources speaking off-record confirm the security detail was neutralized without casualties, which they describe as 'operationally extraordinary.' Tessera CEO Harlan Voss-Kimura issued a statement calling the killing 'an act of terrorism against the institution of enterprise itself' and demanding a Federal Remnant task force. As of this evening, no arrests have been made. The Red Ledger has never been publicly attributed to any known faction.
aftermath: The MME investigation produced no charges within its eighteen-month active period; a leaked Graycloaks intelligence summary circulating in 2139 alleged the contract had been funded by a consortium of former Tessera employees operating through an anonymous Bore Rats financial cutout, but the claim was never verified.
runner_relevance: The Solberg-Faye killing sent an immediate shockwave through the executive protection market. Every major corponation with officers above VP-tier issued emergency contracts for upgraded personal security details within seventy-two hours — protection work paying 8,000 to 15,000 quanta per week per principal. Simultaneously, Tessera hired investigation runners to identify Red Ledger network nodes, offering a reported 200,000 quanta bounty for actionable intelligence on the contracting party. Runners with Arcturus Defense credentials were in particular demand to audit the security breach, and the Graycloaks immediately began brokering information about the kill at premium rates to anyone with enough quanta to ask the right questions.
